requirements.text: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

claude.basis: On net5+ consumers the attribute is emitted on every generated type (AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage passes at head and fails on base). But every emission is wrapped in '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK', which is evaluated in the consumer's compilation, so consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get no attribute. The stated reason ('not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework') is wrong: System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is in the netstandard 2.0 reference assembly (I checked netstandard.library 2.0.3's netstandard.xml) and has been in .NET Framework since 4.0, with AttributeTargets.Class allowed. So for targets MessagePack supports, the requirement is not met, and a test pins the omission.

findings.title: Coverage attribute is suppressed for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework consumers based on a false premise
findings.claim: The templates guard the attribute with '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK'. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, so the guard only removes the feature for Unity/.NET Framework/netstandard library consumers. The test ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable pins this behaviour, and the README claims 'All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated', which is false for those targets.

evidence.quote: All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`
evidence.note: quote matches README.md:1639 at head a0aa5ab2

findings.suggested_fix: Drop the #if guard and emit [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] unconditionally; replace the guard test with one that compiles generated code against a netstandard2.0 / net472 reference set.

findings.claim: 228 of 237 files are regenerated expected-output resources. The behavioural change is in 7 template/source files. Reviewers should read the templates and spot-check the resources, not the reverse.

findings.title: Unrelated formatting change in TransformUtilities.cs outside the requirement scope
findings.claim: TransformUtilities.cs line 58 changed the brace emission for nested types that carry type constraints from emitting just "{" to emitting "{\r\n", adding a newline after the opening brace in generated code. This is unrelated to REQ-2297-F1 (ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) and changes generated output beyond the requirement's scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Revert TransformUtilities.cs to the base line, or move this formatting change to a separate change so this change stays limited to ExcludeFromCodeCoverage emission.

findings.title: Attribute on the generated half of user-declared partial resolvers can break builds (CS0579) and silently hides user code
findings.claim: The resolver and composite resolver templates emit '[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] partial class <ResolverName>' for a class the user declares as partial. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has AllowMultiple = false. A user who already put [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on their partial resolver declaration will get error CS0579 'Duplicate attribute' after upgrading on the targets where the guard is active (I reproduced CS0579 with two partial declarations each carrying the attribute). Even without a conflict, the attribute applies to the whole type, so any hand-written members in the user's partial resolver are now excluded from coverage too.
findings.suggested_fix: On the user-declared partial resolver, put the attribute on the generated members (Instance field, GetFormatter method, nested FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper classes) instead of the type, or skip it when the user's declaration already carries the attribute.
